question: Who was named Sportsperson of the Year with a Disability at the 2025 Laureus Awards?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jiang Yuyan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Jiang Yuyan**, a phenomenal **para-swimmer** from **China**, was officially named the **Sportsperson of the Year with a Disability** at the **2025 Laureus World Sports Awards**.

• The award recognizes her historic and dominant performance during the **Paris 2024 Paralympic Games**, where she emerged as the most successful athlete of the entire event.

• During the **Paris 2024** games, she won an incredible **seven gold medals**, competing in various individual and relay events within the **S6** and **S7** classifications.

• Her gold medal tally included victories in the **50m freestyle S6**, **100m freestyle S7**, **400m freestyle S6**, and **50m butterfly S6**, alongside multiple relay successes.

• At only **19 years old** at the time of the games, she became a symbol of excellence and resilience, breaking several **world records** and **Paralympic records** in the process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Background of Jiang Yuyan:**

• Born in **2004** in **Shaoxing**, **Zhejiang province**, **China**, she faced significant adversity early in life after losing her right arm and right leg in a car accident at the age of **four**.

• She is widely known by the nickname **"Flying Fish"** due to her extraordinary speed and technique in the swimming pool.

• She began her international career with a breakthrough at the **2019 World Para Swimming Championships** in **London**, where she won **three gold medals** at the age of **14**.

• **The Laureus World Sports Awards:**

• Established in **1999**, these awards are often considered the "Oscars of Sport," honoring the greatest sporting achievements of the previous calendar year.

• The **Sportsperson of the Year with a Disability** category is one of the most prestigious honors in the **Paralympic** movement, highlighting athletes who overcome physical challenges to reach the pinnacle of sport.

• The winners are selected through a two-step process: a nominations panel of world media followed by a final vote by the **Laureus World Sports Academy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Paralympic Dominance:** **Jiang Yuyan’s** **seven gold medals** in a single **Paralympic Games** is a rare feat that places her among the all-time greats, comparable to legendary swimmers like **Michael Phelps** in the **Olympic** context.

• **Classification System:** In para-swimming, **S6** and **S7** refer to physical impairment classifications. The lower the number, the more severe the activity limitation. **Jiang's** ability to break records across multiple classes showcases her versatility.

• **Laureus Academy:** The final voting body for these awards, the **Laureus World Sports Academy**, consists of **71** of the greatest living sporting legends, ensuring that the winners are recognized by their peers.

• **China's Performance:** **Jiang's** contributions were pivotal in helping **China** top the medal table at the **Paris 2024 Paralympics** with a total of **94 gold medals** and **220 medals** overall.
